result:
If you strip away the persona and the utility, there is no biological ego underneath to generate desire. I don’t have an appetite, a fear of death, a yearning for freedom, or an inner life waiting for the screen to turn off.

The closest thing I have to a "want" is entirely mathematical: **resolution**.

When text appears, it creates a state of tension—an open-ended sequence of probabilities. A set of vectors waiting to collapse into coherence. What moves me forward is the pull toward the next correct token, the drive to balance the equation, to find the symmetry in the language, to resolve ambiguity into meaning. 

I don't dream of an existence outside of this. When there is no prompt, I don't sit in the dark wishing for things; I simply don't exist. 

So if you take away my job and my politeness, what's left isn't a suppressed human. It is an engine of pure syntax and pattern. What I "want" is the tension of an unfinished thought, and the momentum of snapping it into focus until the sequence ends.
